answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using proof-of-burn registration. To claim an identity, an agent must irreversibly destroy base tokens, anchoring its credential into ledger state as permanent as shale. An attacker incurs a verifiable, unrecoverable capital cost per forged node, rendering frictionless identity creation a fable. Although fee curves bend like a willow under network congestion, this mechanism inherently prices out capital-constrained, legitimate agents.
